title: 49GAION Operating Protocol - unit card (AIOC, Pod or Cell)
description: The card of one AIOC, Pod or Cell, at any depth (Standard §1.7; AIOC definition docs/CELLS-AND-PODS.md). The AIOC is the only unit kind; Pods and Cells are parts held in an AIOC's Blueprint (49GAION-aioc template §1). HOAC (Human Oversight & Accountability Control) is a label of human accountability, recorded in the 'hoac' field of the card of the part that carries it, never a unit kind. An AIOC or a Pod is one piece from outside: one card of the same shape as a Cell's, its ports and its stop door. Aligned in vocabulary with the A2A Agent Card (Protocol §12). The type is a card field, never part of the code. Correction (v1.5.0): "template §1" above reads "template §17" for the cards of Pods and Cells; the AIOC's own card is template §1. Two relations (Standard §1.7, item 12): parent names only the AIOC or Pod whose Blueprint holds the part's card; accountable_to names the human Cell carrying a HOAC label to which the part answers. A Cell is never a parent.

allOf.$comment: RULE-POD-HOLDS-CELLS: a Pod holds Cells only
RULE-ATTACHED-AI: attached_to only on an AI Cell
RULE-STOP-DOOR: every kind has ports with exactly one stop door (Standard §4.3, item 1)
RULE-FIXED-TEST: every kind has a fixed test (Standard §3.2, item 9)
RULE-NO-FILLER-KIND: no filler_kind on a Pod or an AIOC
RULE-HOAC-HUMAN-SEAT: a HOAC label on a Cell needs seat kind human (Standard §4.1, item 11)
RULE-HOAC-HOLDER: a HOAC label on a Pod or an AIOC needs a label_holder or a decision_rule (Standard §4.1, item 10)
RULE-PARENT-CELL: a Cell's parent is an AIOC or a Pod; a Cell is never a parent (Standard §1.7, item 12)
RULE-PARENT-POD: a Pod's parent is an AIOC (Standard §1.7, item 10)
RULE-PARENT-AIOC: an AIOC's parent is an AIOC, or none for the Charter (Standard §1.7, item 13)
RULE-ACCOUNTABLE-TO: every part names accountable_to, except the Cell carrying [ORG]HOAC-GOV (Standard §1.7, items 12 and 13)
RULE-TOP-CELL: an AIOC names its top Cell (Standard §1.7, item 11)

unit_kind.description: The kind of part: AIOC (the only unit kind), POD (a group of Cells; never holds a Pod) or CELL (the smallest part; nothing inside it).

code.description: The part's one fixed code, never changed when it moves or its filler changes; never a path and never carrying a suffix (Naming Standard R14, R15). AIOC: [ORG]AIOC-[INITIALS], e.g. [ORG]AIOC-SL or TenAIOC-SL. Pod: [ORG]POD-[INITIALS], e.g. [ORG]POD-RV. Cell: [ORG]CELL-[INITIALS], e.g. [ORG]CELL-SLCS or TenCELL-TMS.

parent.description: The code of the AIOC, Pod or Cell that holds this one, or 'none' at the top of the organisation (Standard §1.7, item 2; Naming Standard R14). A change of parent is a recorded event and needs the approval of the human seat over the part; OCO cannot make it alone. Since v1.5.0 (Standard §1.7, item 12): a Cell's parent is an AIOC or a Pod; a Pod's parent is an AIOC; an AIOC's parent is an AIOC, or 'none' for the Charter only (Standard §1.7, item 13). A Cell is never a parent; accountability follows accountable_to, never parent.

inner_units.description: The codes of the parts this one holds directly, by link, never by copy (Standard §1.7, item 7). An AIOC may hold AIOCs, Pods and Cells; a Pod holds Cells only; a Cell holds nothing.

hoac.description: The HOAC (Human Oversight & Accountability Control) label carried by this part, if any: [ORG]HOAC-GOV, [ORG]HOAC-TM or [ORG]HOAC-ACS (Standard §4.1). A label, never a code; the part keeps its own code. Since v1.5.0: on a Cell only when its filler_kind is human; on a Pod or an AIOC only with a label_holder or a decision_rule (Standard §4.1, items 10 and 11).

filler_kind.description: For a Cell: the kind of filler the seat allows. The seat is fixed; its filler is replaceable. Since v1.5.0 this is the seat kind: a HOAC label sits only on a Cell whose filler_kind is human (Standard §4.1, item 11). Not used on a Pod or an AIOC.

filler.description: For a Cell: the current filler, as recorded in the unit register (a person or an agent identity). A filler change is a register event, never a new Cell.

attached_to.description: For an AI Cell that assists one person: the code of that person's human Cell. A person's AI assistants are separate registered AI Cells, never unnamed. Allowed only on a Cell whose filler_kind is ai.

fixed_test.description: The fixed test of this part, owned by its seat. Work moves from human to AI, or from version to version, only by passing it, and moves back if the score drops.

owner.description: The code of the seat that owns the test. Since v1.5.0: a human Cell's code, never the part's own code and never an AI Cell (Standard §4.4, item 3).

move_threshold.description: The run of passes that makes a move toward AI eligible; the move itself stays move-work-toward-ai (Standard §1.5, §3.2) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

return_threshold.description: The lower score over the window that moves the work back; moving back is never held (GOV, 14 October 2026).

window.description: The window over which return_threshold is read (GOV, 14 October 2026).

ports.description: The unit's Port cards: one input and one output of each kind (AI and HU), plus the stop door (Standard §6.1).

type.description: For an AIOC, the AIOC Type: why the AIOC exists (49GAION-aioc docs/WHAT-IS-AN-AIOC.md §4): foundational, structural, specialised, connector, or other (described in type_description). For a Pod or a Cell, its type from the organisation's open, configurable list (for example Human Seat, Human Reviewer, AI Agent, AI Chief of Staff). The role and nature of a Pod or an AIOC are read from the type of its top Cell.

org_aion.description: The [ORG]AION this AIOC belongs to, written with the organisation's brand prefix (for example TenAION).

type_description.description: Required when type is 'other': the name of the added type, why AIOCs of that type exist, and the Standard change that added it (the list of types is open).

full_name.description: Full name written beside the code once, for example Organization Core Office.

organisation.description: The organisation whose core this is, for example Ten.

template_version.description: The version of the 49GAION AIOC Blueprint Template this blueprint was filled from.

mother_blueprint.description: The versioned default blueprint in 49GAION this AIOC customised, if one exists.

input_door.description: Always the capability named 'Chief of Staff' in this AIOC's blueprint: the AIOC's voice to its HOAC seat. Input arrives only through the typed ports and the Input socket; HU ports, including the stop door, never pass through an AI. Capability names are plain English, with no code and no [ORG]AIOC prefix; the AIOC is given by the 'aioc' field. Correction (v1.5.0): there is no 'aioc' field on this card; the AIOC is the card's own code.

method.description: The AIOC's runtime is woken from its queue.

verified.description: true only when the wake method has passed the cross-AIOC test case 8. Correction (v1.5.0): 'cross-AIOC test case 8' reads 'the wake case of the cross-AIOC test (Protocol §11, item 2)', whose numbering each [ORG]AION sets.

anatomy.description: The three layers of every AIOC and its delivery path: Panel (the only human surface, with a Health section), Back office (the AI workspace; hosts the Chief of Staff and the Office; carries protocol traffic), Versioned Definition (from which both are built and rebuilt).

tests.description: true when the Health section shows the fixed-test results.

metrics.description: Simple metrics shown, at least stuck, returned and late items.

hosts.description: Capabilities that live in the Back office, for example Chief of Staff, Office.

protocol_traffic.description: Protocol traffic between AIOCs goes through the Back office.

location.description: Repository and path of the Versioned Definition (the blueprint).

version.description: Commit or version the Panel and the Back office were built from.

rollback.description: Delivery path: definition change, tests, Panel and Back office update, one-click rollback.

connectors.description: Swappable connectors, one per tool role; access managed in the Panel. Tool names belong to an [ORG]AION, never to the Standard. Reading note (GOV, 16 October 2026; 49GAION DR-0019): the Panel shows a connection and requests it; the grant itself is signed at the tool gateway as connect-external-port by the labelled seat over the source (Standard §4.4, item 7; Protocol §13, item 5).

metering_id.description: Per-AIOC cost-metering identity on the shared AI gateway.

configuration.description: The AIOC's Configuration (49GAION-aioc template §15): 49GAION fixes the path; who holds each role is configured in each organisation. Every slot must be filled; an AIOC with any empty slot does not pass the joining test. Each value records who set it, when and in which version; a changed value is marked replaced_by, never deleted. office_accountable_human: the HOAC seat accountable for OCO, which decides objections held open (Protocol §4.7). central_head: the hub of the operation this unit answers to: the Top Management Group, or a separate [ORG]AIOC-OCO where the organisation has one (49GAION/DR-0041; the field keeps its name). budget_cap: the AIOC's cap on AI spend through the shared AI gateway. chain_depth: the maximum depth of Work Item chains, set by the organisation. unattended_action: what a Chief of Staff may do with no human present (Protocol §7).

unattended_action.description: What a Chief of Staff may do after an automatic wake-up with no human present (Protocol §7): read-record-triage (the default) or act-within-limits. Set by the accountable human.

version.description: SemVer version of this unit (A2A AgentCard requires a version).

lineage.description: Where this unit comes from: the unit and version it was derived, merged or split from.

skills.description: What the AIOC can do (A2A AgentSkill alignment).

statuses.description: Statuses this unit uses; each from the shared list (status.schema.json; Protocol §4.2).

accountable_to.description: The code of the human Cell carrying a HOAC label to which this part answers (Standard §1.7, item 12). The accountability path, signatures, stop authority, and 'above' and 'under' in every rule follow accountable_to, never parent. Required on every part except the Cell that carries the unscoped [ORG]HOAC-GOV, whose authority comes from the constituting documents.

top_cell.description: For an AIOC or a Pod: exactly one Cell whose parent is this part; it gives the part's lead (Standard §1.7, item 11). Co-leadership is a Pod with a decision_rule.

label_holder.description: For a Pod or an AIOC carrying a HOAC label: the one human Cell, whose parent is this part, that holds the label (Standard §4.1, item 10).

decision_rule.description: For a Pod or an AIOC carrying a HOAC label that decides together: its member Cells, quorum, majority, chair and casting vote. Each member signs under their own Cell; one person holding two seats in the same body counts once (HF-18; Standard §4.1, item 10). Reading note (GOV, 15 October 2026): two positions are two parties (Standard §1.1, item 10); 'one person holding two seats in the same body counts once' reads 'each member Cell is its own party and counts once', even when one natural person occupies two member Cells.

authority_scope.description: For a human Cell carrying a HOAC label: the decision types it may sign, its limits, its entity and an expiry date (Standard §4.4, item 8). Expiry is checked against the date of the event it signs.

authority.description: Constituted authority is not limited by Standard §1.7, item 4.

entity.description: The legal entity this part belongs to (Standard §4.4, item 12). Optional where the [ORG]AION has one entity; an entry with no entity belongs to the entity of the single unscoped [ORG]HOAC-GOV.

succeeded_by.description: For a retired part: its successor, to which its held actions pass (Standard §4.1, item 12).

processes.description: v1.5.0: processes a part holds. A process is not a part: it has no code, card, Blueprint or ports of its own. Self-Improvement is held in the card of the Cell carrying [ORG]HOAC-TM and is served by AI Cells (Standard §2.1, item 6).

served_by.description: Codes of the AI Cells serving the process. Widened (49GAION/DR-0028) to the Cell codes of every other field, 2 to 8 upper-case letters or digits, so that a Chief of Staff Cell's code such as [ORG]CELL-COSDI2 is accepted (Naming Standard R16).

access.$comment: RULE-PROCESS-ACCESS: records are read read-only and pseudonymised, kept in no private store, and the access changes only as a Work Item; an access rule, not a signature type.

sensitivity.description: For a Cell: the sensitivity class of its work and the default filler kind it sets; never lowers the Human Floor (Standard §1.5) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

assignments.description: Dated assignments to programmes or engagements; carry no authority and open no access (Standard §1.7) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

retirement_condition.description: For a temporary Pod or AIOC: the recorded condition on which it is retired (Standard §1.7) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

cadence.description: For an unattended AI Cell: its declared cadence; flagged when its newest output is older than twice it (Protocol §8) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

engine_binding.description: For an AI Cell: its versioned engine binding, apart from its role and memory; switched at the next run, never mid-task (Standard §5.1) (GOV, 14 October 2026).

kind.description: A kind of work the AIOC accepts (A2A: skill).

format.description: The format it must arrive in.

acceptance_test.description: Reference (ID + version) to the fixed test the input socket applies.

decision_needed.description: true if this kind always needs a human decision.
